before: The switch expression chooses a result using case labels. The -> form supplies a result for a matching arm without old-style fallthrough.
default provides the result when none of the listed labels match. A result-producing switch must cover its permitted inputs.
The value of this entire switch expression becomes action. The chosen String can then be used like any other value.
Expected output or behavior: Write. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Add one supported choice and test both it and an unknown value. Keep an intentional fallback. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: An expression produces a value. A switch expression compares its input with case labels and chooses a result. The arrow form, ->, uses the matching case without continuing into the next case.
default handles values that do not match a listed case. A switch expression must cover every input allowed for that switch so it can produce a result.
Here, the whole switch produces one String. Java stores that String in action, ready for the print statement.
The program prints Write. choice is two, so the second case supplies that text.
The quiz uses a number that neither listed case matches. Follow the default case to find the result.
